summary.text:
Charnwood is a small district with a clean, small book. All 22 external PWLB loans are HRA; the General Fund carries none. Total external debt £76.19m at 3.38% weighted, 12.6 years average life (page 8). CFR £103.525m; internal borrowing £27.335m by the balance-sheet identity, which ties to their own 'Under borrowing' line to the £000. No PFI, no finance leases, no LOBOs, no market debt, no bank loans — nothing to strip out.

The loan book reconciles cleanly: our file agrees £76,190,000 of PWLB principal to the £000, across 22 maturity loans. The coupon-weighted rate is 3.4254% against their 3.38% — a 4-5 basis point gap consistent with effective-interest presentation rather than a book difference. And on rescheduling, their section 5 statement that the approximate 1% differential between PWLB new-borrowing and premature-repayment rates made rescheduling unviable is a specific, testable claim: our engine puts about £12.3m of latent discount across the book (16% of principal, every one of the 22 loans below par), but replacement at today's certainty curve would raise running cost by roughly two percentage points against their weighted 3.38%. On straight arithmetic their read holds.

The paper flags an autumn 2026 update to the Capital Plan, including a section on future financing options — the borrowing decision has been deferred, not avoided. £4.97m of HRA capex went unfinanced in the year, and about £4m of PWLB rolls off in the next 24 months. Investment book halved in the year from £37.4m to £16.2m; the council moved from net-investor to net-debtor. Pooled property is fully exited (Federated Hermes PUT and Lothbury both wound up during the year at losses of £343k and £700k, both fully provided for). Investments earned 4.467% against the SONIA 90-day benchmark of 4.124%, an out-performance of 34 bps on a £37m average balance.

officer.subject: 22 loans, £76.19m to the £000 — and your rescheduling arithmetic checks out
officer.body:
Hi Neil,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the Q4 outturn that went to Audit Committee on 7 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Yours is a short and cleanly written report; this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

A cross-check first, and yours is one of the tidier reconciliations we've read. Your table on page 8 gives HRA external debt of £76.19m at 3.38% weighted with 12.6 years average life. Our file has 22 PWLB loans totalling £76,190,000 — the principal ties to the £000. The coupon-weighted rate we get is 3.4254%; the 4-5 basis point gap against your 3.38% is the signature of an effective-interest-rate presentation on your side against coupon-weighting on ours, not a book difference. And the balance-sheet identity closes without needing to strip anything out: CFR £103.525m less external £76.190m less zero long-term liabilities leaves £27.335m, which is exactly the Under borrowing line on page 7. Books that tie this cleanly are rarer than they should be.

The reason we wrote is one sentence in section 5. On rescheduling, you note that the approximate 1% differential between PWLB new borrowing rates and premature repayment rates made it unviable. That is a specific, testable statement and we can price it. Against the DMO's premature repayment curve today, every one of the 22 loans sits below par — about £12.3m of latent discount, roughly 16% of the book. But most of that discount sits on the four long-dated loans maturing between 2047 and 2061, and replacing those on the certainty curve at your own year-end would cost 6.29% at twenty-five years and 6.08% at fifty, against a book weighted at 3.38%. On a like-for-like basis the higher running cost swamps the up-front discount inside a couple of years, exactly as your paper reads it. Standard caveats and we mean them — we don't sell treasury products, only the DMO can quote binding numbers, and we model no MRP or accounting treatment. But on straight arithmetic your observation holds.

Where the picture might change is the autumn Capital Plan update your report flags on page 12. Whatever comes into it will need pricing against the curve on the day, not the curve at the strategy sign-off. The place to watch that is pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity, which publishes every loan the sector draws each month with a note on what moved. Borrower counts have been thin over the summer, which usually means the inter-authority market gets expensive alongside — and worth knowing before you term out, not after.

Your own book is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis, priced daily.

On training, three fit Charnwood. Strategic PWLB borrowing, for the autumn financing decision. HRA treasury — because 100% of your external book is HRA and the HRA rate is gilt plus 40 basis points against gilt plus 80 on certainty, which matters when you next go long. And PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator, for the arithmetic you already ran in section 5. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
